sentences.text:
NOTE 02. 25.02.2026 BVLNC,J I.A.No.01 of 2026 Heard learned counsel representing Sri Katha Siva Sai Chandra Subhash, learned counsel for the petitioner/appellant/convict and Sri A.Sai Rohith,
learned Assistant Public Prosecutor representing the State.

Petitioner is accused No.1 in S.C.No.16 of 2025 on the file of the learned V Additional District and Sessions Judge-cum-Special Court for Trial of the Offences against Women, West Godavari District at Eluru.
Learned counsel for the  petitioner/appellant would submit that petitioner/convict was found guilty for the offence under Sections 417 & 376(2)(n) of IPC.

Accordingly, he was convicted U/s.235(2) Cr.P.C. and sentenced to undergo rigorous imprisonment for a period of ten (10) years and to pay a fine of Rs.5,000/- (Rupees Five Thousand only) in default,
shall undergo simple imprisonment for a period of two (02) months for the offence under Section (Contd..) 376(2)(n) of IPC.
He further sentenced to undergo imprisonment for a period of six (06) months for the offence under Section 417 of IPC.
Both sentences shall run concurrently.
Learned counsel for the petitioner/appellant/convict would further submit that the petitioner/convict paid the fine amount and filed original receipt along with the appeal grounds.
The learned counsel for the petitioner/appellant/convict would submit that the learned trial Court erroneously convicted the petitioner without appreciating the facts in proper perspective.
Hence, the petitioner preferred the appeal, challenging the judgment on various grounds.
He would further submit that the petitioner was on bail during trial and before and there are no allegations of breach of bail bonds.

He would further submit that the sentence imposed by the learned trial Court is a fixed sentence for a period of ten (10) years, and there is a fair chance to succeed in the appeal, and there is no possibility of hearing the appeal in the near future, and the order of sentence of imprisonment imposed by the trial Court may be suspended, pending disposal of the appeal.
(Contd...)
Learned Assistant Public Prosecutor opposed the application.
However, no written objections filed.
He fairly conceded that the petitioner was on bail during trial an before.

Considering the above submissions, facts of the case and as the sentence imposed by the trial Court CRLA/92/2026 on 25 February, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/95899769/
1 is a fixed sentence of ten (10) years and as there is no possibility of hearing the appeal in the near future, "the order of sentence of imprisonment alone imposed by the learned V Additional District and Sessions Judge-cum-Special Court for Trial of the Offences against Women, West Godavari District at Eluru, vide judgment dated 02.02.2026 in S.C.No.16 of 2025 shall be suspended, pending disposal of the appeal, subject to the following conditions":
i) The petitioner/appellant/accused shall be enlarged on bail, on executing a personal bond for Rs.25,000/- (Rupees Twenty Five Thousand only), with two (02) sureties for a like sum each, to the satisfaction of the learned trial Court.
ii) On such release, the petitioner/ appellant/accused shall appear before the learned trial Court, on every fourth Saturday of the month, till disposal of the Appeal.
iii) The petitioner/appellant/accused shall not intimidate or annoy or contact the victim in any manner.
iv) The petitioner/appellant/accused shall not leave the country without permission of the Court.
v) If the petitioner/appellant/accused violates any of the above conditions, the prosecution is at liberty to file an application seeking cancellation of the bail.
Accordingly, the application is ordered.
BVLNC,J Heard.
Admit the appeal.
Call for Trial Court record.
Registry is directed to prepare paper booklet, as soon as trial Court record is received.
List the matter in the last week of June, 2026, in usual course.
